title: The Unread Manuscript
text:
In the declining years of the old century, the library of Harrowgate Manor stood silent, its leather volumes gathering a patina of dust that no servant had the diligence to remove. Its master, Lord Ashcombe, had long since retired to the country, and he rarely deigned to return to the chambers where his grandfather had once received the most eminent scholars of the realm. Yet the manuscript he had left behind was not forgotten; it was whispered of in drawing-rooms as an account of a voyage undertaken by a sailor who claimed to have seen the coast of a land absent from every chart.

The sailor's narrative, written in a hand that grew increasingly tremulous towards its close, described a harbour of white stone and a people who measured the passage of time by the falling of petals rather than the turning of the sun. Scholars who examined the pages disagreed sharply upon their veracity, some dismissing them as the fanciful inventions of a man in fever, others insisting that the particularity of the detail argued for an honest, if bewildered, witness. What is certain is that the manuscript has since passed through many hands, each reader adding a marginal note that betrays more of his own convictions than of the sailor's.

questions.text: How did the people in the sailor's account measure the passage of time?
options: By the bells of a tower
By the movement of the tides
By the phases of the moon

questions.text: What can be inferred about the scholars' attitude toward the manuscript?
options: They were divided and cautious about whether it was true
They unanimously accepted every detail of the account
They believed Lord Ashcombe had written it himself
They had destroyed the pages long ago

questions.text: What does the final sentence suggest about the readers of the manuscript?
options: They read the text through their own convictions
They were all sailors who had visited the land
They had no interest in the manuscript at all
They copied the sailor's account exactly as written

vocabulary.definition: a thin layer that forms on a surface over a long period of time
shaking or trembling slightly, usually from nervousness or weakness
the quality of being true and accurate
written or located in the margin of a page

paragraph_translations: Yüzyılın son yıllarında Harrowgate Malikanesi'nin kütüphanesi sessiz duruyordu; deri ciltli kitapları, hiçbir hizmetlinin temizlemeye özen göstermediği bir toz tabakasıyla kaplanıyordu. Malikanenin sahibi Lord Ashcombe çoktan kırsala çekilmişti ve büyükbabasının ülkenin en seçkin bilginlerini ağırladığı odalara nadiren dönerdi. Yine de geride bıraktığı el yazması unutulmuş değildi; salonlarda, her haritada yeri olmayan bir kıyıyı gördüğünü iddia eden bir denizcinin yolculuk anlatısı olarak fısıltıyla anılıyordu.

Denizcinin anlatımı, sonlara doğru giderek titreyen bir el yazısıyla yazılmıştı; beyaz taştan bir liman ile zamanı güneşin dönüşüyle değil, çiçek yapraklarının düşüşüyle ölçen bir halkı tarif ediyordu. Sayfaları inceleyen bilginler doğruluğu konusunda keskin biçimde ayrıştılar: bazıları bunları ateş içindeki bir adamın hayal ürünü sayarken, bazıları ayrıntıların özgüllüğünün dürüst, ama şaşkın bir tanığa işaret ettiğinde ısrar ediyordu. Kesin olan şu ki el yazması o zamandan beri birçok elden geçti ve her okur, denizcinin inançlarından çok kendi inançlarını ele veren bir kenar notu ekledi.
